metadata.note: The Georgia Southern and Florida (Macon - Valdosta - Lake City - Palatka, opened 1889-1890, and the ex-Atlantic, Valdosta and Western Valdosta - Jacksonville line it bought in 1902), with the AV&W's own 1899-1902 years and two affiliated roads that ran trains under their own names: the Macon and Birmingham (Macon - LaGrange, 1891-1922) and the Hawkinsville and Florida Southern (a single-year 1895 anchor). Every feature is drawn only for the report's drawable span; avw-valdosta-jacksonville and gsf-valdosta-jacksonville share identical geometry (Rule 4 split at the 1902 sale).
metadata.ownership_split: AV&W -> GS&F at the May 1902 sale (Southern control 1 July 1902): SPLIT. NOT splits: the 1895 Railroad -> Railway reorganization under Southern stock control (same display name; the GS&F kept running its own trains, GS&F-lettered locomotives photographed 1911/1916, its own 1918 timetable). Southern's named through trains (Royal Palm, Ponce de Leon) ran over GS&F track but the line features stay GS&F colour for their whole span; no date was found at which Southern began operating the GS&F directly - if one is found, split there. Macon and Birmingham and Hawkinsville and Florida Southern: GS&F ownership / stock control, but each ran trains under its own name - own company and colour.
metadata.omitted: Hawkinsville and Florida Southern Davisville - Fitzgerald branch: drawable NONE (no confirmed passenger year). Augusta Southern: not GS&F, drawn under its own report. Southern Railway's named through trains (Royal Palm, Ponce de Leon) over the GS&F: not drawn as separate features - they belong to a Southern Railway research file. Southern's own Macon - Jesup - Jacksonville and Atlanta - Macon lines are not GS&F and not drawn here.
metadata.freight_only: Excluded under Rule 1: the AV&W's ~45 mi of spurs (mostly logging in southern Clinch County); Craig Junction - Calhoun (an 1898 Guide listing that predates the AV&W, likely a logging stop, no confirmable passenger year); Vickers Junction; the Statenville Railway; post-passenger freight on every line (NS still runs Macon - Valdosta, Valdosta - Navair and Valdosta - Jacksonville; Lake City - Palatka carried freight to the late 1980s) - context only.
not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] ends: Valdosta - Lake City and Lake City - Palatka are drawn to 1951, the last CONFIRMED year (Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 15 mixed train); when the mixed train actually ended is unknown. ICC / Florida RR & Public Utilities Commission discontinuance orders, a 1950s Southern public timetable or local 'last train' stories would settle it.
Whether the 1951 mixed train ran end-to-end Valdosta - Palatka or only part: read as end-to-end, but the Guide OCR is too mangled to state the pattern.
Macon - Valdosta end 1967 is single-sourced (Wikipedia's Royal Palm article citing the Sept 1967 Official Guide); Valdosta - Jacksonville 1966 has two sources but Wikipedia's sentence is ambiguous.
1890 start for Valdosta - Palatka is collapsed from 'completed March 1890'; part may have opened in 1889.
[ANCHOR] Hawkinsville and Florida Southern Hawkinsville - Worth: 1895 only; railga's 1897/1906/1918 timetables could not be viewed.
Royal Palm start year and the date its routing began over the GS&F: not established. Kansas City - Florida Special routing over the GS&F conflicts with a 1922 schedule via Jesup - not used.
When (if ever before 1982) Southern began operating the GS&F directly - the only thing that could force a Rule 4 split on the GS&F features.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates.
source_conflicts: Macon and Birmingham ownership: railga.com (GS&F-owned from the start, separate accounts) vs Wikipedia (GS&F acquired it in 1902). Does not change the span or the company.
Valdosta - Jacksonville passenger end: Wikipedia's Royal Palm sentence (1966) may refer to dropping the diner/sleeper rather than the segment; chicagorailfan.com independently gives 1966.

properties.line: Georgia Southern and Florida: Macon – Valdosta
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE: ~45 km/h average for a south Georgia main line carrying through Cincinnati - Jacksonville trains; no timetable times were converted
geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via the maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror (railway degree-tiles + old_railway_operator ways), routed with opstrace.py, 2026-11-09
properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap: today's Norfolk Southern (ex-Southern / GS&F) Macon - Valdosta line, ways tagged old_railway_operator=Southern where OSM carries the tag. Routed with opstrace.py (mileage by OSM tag: own-road ways (OSM old_railway_operator=Southern, or OHM ways named for the GS&F) 151.2 mi, untagged rail 0.3 mi, CoG 0.0 mi). Traced 151.5 mi against 151.3 mi (Fowler GA sec. 105, Macon Terminal - Valdosta 2nd station) documented. No straight-line leg. Every waypoint (Macon Terminal Station, Bonaire, Kathleen, Unadilla, Vienna, Cordele, Ashburn, Tifton, Sparks, Adel, Hahira, Valdosta) lies within 1.2 km of the drawn line. LATER ALIGNMENT: drawn on the line as it survives in OSM (modern NS track) and into Macon Terminal Station, which opened in 1916; 1889-1916 trains used Macon Union Depot nearby, a terminal approach not backed out here. Realignments since 1889 are not backed out.

segments.note: Opened Macon - Valdosta February 1889 by the Georgia Southern and Florida Railroad (chartered 1885; receivership 1891; reorganized 1895 as the Georgia Southern and Florida Railway under Southern Railway stock control - treated as one company, since the GS&F kept running its own trains and published its own timetables). Fowler lists most stations '1893t' (z). The Dec 14 1951 Official Guide prints Table 13 'Chattanooga, Atlanta, Macon, Valdosta and Jacksonville (Atlanta Division and G.S.&F. Ry.)' with legible Macon and Valdosta times in the Southern through-car panels (e.g. 1245 AM lv. Macon / 530 AM lv. Valdosta). Southern's Ponce de Leon used the line from 1924 (Wikipedia) and the Royal Palm at least by 1951; the Cordele Dispatch of 21 Sep 1924 lists GS&F local departures to Macon, Jacksonville, Palatka and Valdosta. Years between 1889 and 1951 are drawn as continuous between the opening and the 1951 Guide. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (about two to four trains each way), not a sourced headway.
sources: Segment-level: per the research report, opening Feb 1889 from railga.com and Wikipedia; Dec 1951 service from the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 13 and Southern through-car panels; 1924 GS&F local departures from the Cordele Dispatch 21 Sep 1924 p8
Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (schedules of Dec 14 1951), as cached in research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt

segments.note: Southern's Ponce de Leon dropped its Atlanta - Jacksonville leg in 1964 (Wikipedia); the Royal Palm was cut between Jacksonville and Valdosta in 1966 and, per Wikipedia citing the Official Guide of Sept 1967, discontinued south of Atlanta in summer 1967 - the last passenger train over the GS&F. The 1967 end is single-sourced (Wikipedia's Royal Palm article); the conservative fallback, if a reviewer wants a second source, is 1966. Freight continues today as Norfolk Southern's Macon District - context only, not drawn. headway_min is an ESTIMATE, not a sourced headway.
sources: Segment-level: per the research report, Wikipedia's Royal Palm article (citing Official Guides of Aug 1958 and Sept 1967) for the 1966/1967 cuts and Wikipedia's Ponce de Leon article for 1964; no primary 1952-1967 timetable was read

segments.note: [OPEN END] Part of the GS&F's original Macon - Palatka main line, completed to Palatka March 1890 (railga.com; Fowler lists Lake Park, Melrose, Jennings, Jasper, Genoa, White Springs, Suwannee Valley and Lake City '1893t'). 1890 is the collapsed opening year; part of the line may have opened in 1889, not established. After 1902 through Florida traffic went via the ex-AV&W Jacksonville line; the Cordele Dispatch of 21 Sep 1924 still lists Jacksonville-Palatka departures. Passenger (mixed) service confirmed to Dec 1951 by the Feb 1952 Official Guide, Table 15 'Valdosta and Palatka (G.S.&F.)', dated Dec 14 1951, train header 'Mix', legible times at Valdosta, Lake Park and Jennings and further down the table. 1951 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when the mixed train actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Freight continues today (NS, Valdosta - Navair) - context only. headway_min is an ESTIMATE, not a sourced headway.

The end year is NOT sourced - 1951 is the last confirmed year.

properties.geometry_quality: Lifted late 1980s. Traced where OSM still maps the grade (rail-trail / abandoned-railway ways, chiefly the Palatka - Lake Butler State Trail) and on surviving track at the ends. Routed with opstrace.py (mileage by OSM tag: own-road ways (OSM old_railway_operator=Southern, or OHM ways named for the GS&F) 58.7 mi, untagged path on the grade 10.2 mi, trail:Palatka-Lake Butler State Trail 4.0 mi, connector joins under 300 m 0.2 mi). Traced 73.1 mi against 73.4 mi (Fowler 211.6 -> 285.0) documented. No straight-line leg. Lake City - Lake Butler follows an OpenHistoricalMap railway way named 'Georgia Southern & Florida Railroad'; Lake Butler - Palatka follows the Palatka - Lake Butler State Trail (OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=Southern) and, between Lake Butler and Hampton where the trail is not named in OSM, three untagged OSM paths on the grade (ways 421485364, 1153857750, 1153857749), joined by connectors under 300 m. Waypoints Lake Butler, Hampton, Keystone Heights and Florahome lie within 0.5 km of the line. LATER ALIGNMENT: the Palatka end is drawn to the line's OSM alignment into Palatka; before 1908 the GS&F used its own depot at Laurel & Front Sts rather than the ACL union depot, a terminal approach not backed out here.

segments.note: [OPEN END] Completed to Palatka March 1890 (railga.com; Fowler lists Lake Butler, New River, Sampson City, Hampton, Putnam Hall, Grandin, Baywood and Palatka '1893t'). GS&F trains used the ACL union depot at Palatka from 1908. Passenger (mixed) service confirmed to Dec 1951 by the Feb 1952 Official Guide, Table 15 'Valdosta and Palatka (G.S.&F.)', dated Dec 14 1951, train header 'Mix', legible times at mileposts ~102-108 from Valdosta (Keystone Heights) and near Springside; the Guide index places Lake Butler, New River, Keystone Heights, Florahome and Carraway on Table 15 with no freight-only dagger. 1951 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when the mixed train actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. The line was abandoned in the late 1980s; that abandonment year is NOT a passenger end year. headway_min is an ESTIMATE, not a sourced headway.

The AV&W's ~45 mi of spurs, mostly logging lines in southern Clinch County, carried no confirmed passengers and are not drawn. headway_min is an ESTIMATE, not a sourced headway.

properties.geometry_quality: Lifted 1922-23. The first 7.9 mi (Macon - Sofkee) is GS&F track, still in OSM, and the trace is shared with gsf-macon-valdosta there. West of Sofkee the trace uses whatever OSM / OpenHistoricalMap still map of the grade. Routed with opstrace.py (mileage by OSM tag: OHM:(untagged) 83.4 mi, straight line 11.9 mi, own-road ways (OSM old_railway_operator=Southern, or OHM ways named for the GS&F) 8.0 mi, OHM:Thomaston & Barnesville 0.8 mi, untagged rail 0.2 mi, CoG 0.0 mi). Traced 101.9 mi against 104.6 mi (Fowler sec. 112: 96.7 Sofkee - LaGrange + 7.9 over the GS&F Macon - Sofkee; railga '105-mile route') documented. APPROXIMATED legs (straight lines): Sofkee - Lizella 11.6 mi; Woodbury (end of Macon - Woodbury trace) - Woodbury (start of Woodbury - LaGrange trace) 0.3 mi. Macon - Sofkee (7.9 mi) is the GS&F, today's NS Macon District, shared with gsf-macon-valdosta. Lizella - LaGrange follows untagged OpenHistoricalMap railway ways, which coincide with the OSM abandoned way named 'Macon & Birmingham Railroad' west of Lizella; Lizella, Yatesville, Thomaston, Woodbury, Odessadale, Mountville and LaGrange all lie within 0.6 km of the line (Culloden 1.8 km). Sofkee - Lizella (12.8 mi per Fowler) is mapped in neither OSM nor OHM. SOURCE CONFLICT: OHM maps an untagged railway (way 202209986) running directly west from Macon to Lizella, bypassing Sofkee; the report (Fowler) says M&B trains ran over the GS&F to Sofkee, so the trace follows Fowler. The line was traced in two parts joined at Woodbury. LATER ALIGNMENT: the Macon end is drawn into Terminal Station (opened 1916); 1891-1916 trains used Macon Union Depot.
properties.documented_mileage: 104.6 mi (Fowler GA sec. 112 + GS&F Macon - Sofkee)

segments.note: 'The LaGrange Route' / 'Pine Mountain Route'. Completed January 1891 (railga.com; Wikipedia 'operated from 1891'; Fowler tags most stations '1902t' and Thundering Springs, Harris City, Odessa and LaGrange '1893t'); M&B trains ran over the GS&F from Macon Terminal to Sofkee (7.9 mi). Drawn as its own company and colour, not GS&F: it ran trains under its own name with separate accounts. Ownership conflict recorded: railga.com says it was owned by the GS&F from the start, Wikipedia says the GS&F acquired it in 1902. Two passenger trains into Macon until a court order of 29 Jul 1922 let one be dropped (Cordele Dispatch 30 Jul 1922); all services closed 15 Nov 1922 by court order (Cordele Dispatch 14 Nov 1922); dismantled 1922-23 (Americus Times-Recorder 3 Nov 1922). headway_min is an ESTIMATE from the two trains each way, not a sourced headway.
sources: Segment-level: per the research report, 1891 opening from railga.com and Wikipedia; 1922 end from the Cordele Dispatch of 30 Jul 1922 p1 and 14 Nov 1922 p1 and the Americus Times-Recorder of 3 Nov 1922 p1

properties.geometry_quality: Lifted 1923. Traced where OSM / OpenHistoricalMap still map the grade. Routed with opstrace.py (mileage by OSM tag: own-road ways (OSM old_railway_operator=Southern, or OHM ways named for the GS&F) 33.5 mi, OHM:(untagged) 7.3 mi, connector joins under 300 m 0.1 mi). Traced 40.7 mi against 42.3 mi (Fowler sec. 109, Hawkinsville - Worth; railga 43) documented. No straight-line leg. Finleyson - Amboy - Worth follows an OSM abandoned railway (way 164879064, tagged old_railway_operator=Southern) that passes within 0.1 km of Finleyson, Pineview and Amboy, all H&FS stations per Fowler; Hawkinsville - Finleyson follows untagged OpenHistoricalMap railway ways. segments.note: [ANCHOR] Hawkinsville and Florida Southern (ex-Flint River & Gulf), a GS&F stock-controlled road that ran trains under its own name - so its own company and colour. railga.com: 'By 1895 it was also hauling general freight along with passengers on freight trains' (mixed trains); common-carrier charter 1896. 1895 is the ONLY confirmed passenger year: service certainly ran wider both ways (railga hosts 1897/1906/1918 timetables that could not be viewed), but no other year is confirmed. Do not widen without evidence; do not delete to tidy the map. Leased to the Gulf Line 1907; Hawkinsville - Worth abandoned 1923 - an abandonment year, not a passenger end. Trains reached Ashburn over 3.3 mi of GS&F trackage rights (not drawn). headway_min is an ESTIMATE (one mixed train), not a sourced headway.
sources: Segment-level: per the research report, railga.com hawfs.html for mixed passenger service by 1895; no timetable was read
